chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The Imam does not die until he knows who will be after him, so he bequeaths to him.

key_terms.إِلَيْهِ: to him, referring to the succeeding Imam
key_terms.فَيُوصِيَ: so he bequeaths or appoints by testament

ai.seo_question: How does an Imam know who will succeed him after his death?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Imam knows the Imam who will succeed him before his death. It indicates an entrusted and continuous transmission of authority through designation and bequest.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Abdullah Bin Ab Yafour, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdyllah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘An Imam<sup>asws</sup> does not pass away until he<sup>asws</sup> knows one would happen to be (an Imam<sup>asws</sup>) after him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> bequeaths to him<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from ibn Mahbub from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from ‘Abdallah ibn abu Ya‘fur from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
“The does not die until he learns who the succeeding Imams is so he would deliver his will to him.”
